diagnosticHistory.E1: Routing recovered all 78 printable contacts; eight local cap-neighborhood overlap flags motivated finite-width fitting.
diagnosticHistory.E2Classic: Two short model-root necks had no emitted support paths, despite witnesses for all 17 model starts; rejected.
diagnosticHistory.E2Arachne: Recovered one root; the other failed its early-foundation check; diagnostic only.
diagnosticHistory.E3Classic: The wider generic fitting preference preserved both missing roots in the installed-GUI Classic slice. Final acceptance uses this exact Classic export.

knownLimits: These are digital checks for an experimental print, not proof of adhesion, strength, surface quality or clean removal.
The first-emission audit excludes connected expanding overhangs and established bridges. Three sub-layer contacts near the base remain explicitly omitted.
9 very short cavity contacts lack a long pre-cap neck to audit separately; their model-root extrusion checks and local contact review remain explicit.
Short model-root supports attach directly to the miniature. They may leave pits or pull off surface detail during removal; no positive bottom release gap is designed into H0.

One shallow cavity (contact 63) retains its original short pillar because the finite-width fitter found no solution. Its actual extrusion and model foundation pass the path check, but its complete requested geometric clearance is not proven.

One long contact (26) retains about 0.0046 mm sampled local rim penetration. Total measured support/model intersection is about 0.00190 mm³, confined to contact neighborhoods; clean release at every tip is not established.

The engine still warns about two small near-base overhang regions, a 23.7 mm tall support on a 0.24 mm model pad, inaccessible/wedged cavity contacts, and a 0.06 mm² support overhang across one layer near Z28.89. These are retained strength, sag and removal questions for this challenge print.

The minimum 5% nearest-start-overlap screen is an inspection heuristic, not a calibrated print-success threshold. The three remaining sliver flags have 36–44% support overlap one layer lower and stay visible in the review.

Classic and Arachne diagnostics are preserved locally. Only the supplied installed-GUI Classic export passed the complete final audit; results from another profile or re-slice must not be assumed identical.
Nominal bead footprints and layer-envelope gaps are not measured molten-bead air gaps.
This compares the complete custom support package with native normal/snug supports. Individual improvement attribution comes from the separate coupon study.
The original 21-specimen plate remains unchanged. No experimental algorithm changes have been deployed.
